The City of Laredo and Webb County serve largely the same residents and taxpayers, lobby many of the same state and federal officials, and jointly underpin a cross-border trade economy that KGNS describes as the nation's top inland port, with more than $350 billion in trade and an estimated 20,000 commercial trucks crossing daily. Yet the two governments have not always spoken with one voice — and a KGNS panel discussion published October 25 put that complicated relationship under the microscope.

The panel brought together former Laredo Councilmember Gene Belmares and former Webb County Commissioner Jerry Garza, who is the county judge-elect. According to KGNS, the two described a relationship that was once acrimonious and talked about efforts to find common ground between City Hall and the County Courthouse.

One recurring problem the panel raised, according to KGNS, was mixed messages and competing interests when city and county leaders travel to Washington, D.C., to press the region's case — two delegations from the same community, not always carrying the same ask.

The discussion also turned to the proposed 4/5 Bridge, including whether it will be built and why the panelists believe earlier city managers would not have allowed the project to move forward. KGNS notes a functional split at the heart of the city-county dynamic: one government owns the bridges, the other owns the roads leading to them.

Garza, according to KGNS, also discussed an interlocal agreement he would pursue in his first 100 days in office, and a missed opportunity for both governments to work together. The station's written report introduces those topics without publishing the panel's specific grade for the relationship, the specific agreement, or a dated decision on the bridge.

The stakes go beyond personalities. When the city and the county pull in different directions, the region's pitch in Austin and Washington, its border infrastructure, and the services residents receive on both sides of the city-county line all feel the strain. When they align, the same shared tax base and the same trade economy give Laredo and Webb County unusual leverage.

Sources: KGNS, "Sometimes, it's complicated: Inside the relationship status between the City of Laredo and Webb County over the years," October 25, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: A KGNS panel with former Councilmember Gene Belmares and county judge-elect Jerry Garza examined the City of Laredo–Webb County relationship — once acrimonious, now searching for common ground — including mixed messages in Washington and the proposed 4/5 Bridge.
title: 'Sometimes, it's complicated': KGNS panel examines the Laredo–Webb County relationship
